title: Late Breaking Results: Power Rail Routing for Advanced Multi-Layered Printed Circuit Boards
problem: Ultra-wide power rails required for modern high current/voltage demands consume excessive routing area and create overlapping regions. Routing must satisfy IR drop constraints while minimizing metal area and via usage.
motivation: Increasing current and voltage demands in modern PCBs make efficient power rail routing critical to prevent routing congestion and electrical violations.
method: The system sizes power rails according to how much current and voltage each needs to carry, spreading them across the PCB layers to avoid overlaps. If overlaps still occur, an intelligent pathfinding algorithm (like GPS routing, but aware of electrical resistance) automatically reroutes the conflicting rails. This minimizes both the resistance impact and the total routing cost, while keeping the voltage drop across the power distribution within acceptable limits.
key_novelty: The core idea combines sizing power rails by electrical demand with resistance-aware pathfinding to automatically resolve overlaps on multi-layer circuit boards.
contributions: Overlap-aware rail sizing technique for adaptive power rail space allocation
Resistance-aware A*-search algorithm for rail detouring
49% metal area reduction and 28% runtime improvement versus prior art

metrics.other: zero IR drop and current/voltage violations

limitations: Scalability to extremely dense routing scenarios and applicability beyond PCB-level routing are not discussed.
primary_theme: Power rail routing optimization for advanced multi-layer PCBs
